Commentary.Commentary: Archer and Mahmood were brilliant with the new ball. Liam Livingstone was excellent in the middle overs and Dan Mousley impressred too. They'll be a tad disappointed to let Windies cross the 150-run mark but they'll back themselves to chase this. Can they make it 2-0 or will Windies fight back? We will find out.
Powell continued but he too was dismissed when it was time to go big. Shepherd and Forde through have taken their side close to 160 which looked difficult at one stage.

A middling score then for West Indies! They have done well to get to where they are though. The wicket initially played a lot of tricks and hence, they lost three in the Powerplay. Powell and Pooran then steadied the ship but as they looked to accelerate, Pooran fell.
Just the one to end! On the pads. Forde looks to flick but misses. This hits the pad and rolls on the off side. A leg bye taken.

With injuries affecting England as Reece Topley is likely to miss out, this matchup promises to be exciting as the Windies will look to level the series. Windies on the other hand, will be rearing to hit back strong. Their approach in the first game was quite strange and we might see a different one this time. There were positives in their last game but they’ll be eager to put in a complete show here.

Welcome to the second T20I of the five-match series between West Indies and England at the iconic Kensington Oval in Bridgetown, Barbados! A rampant Salt 100 helped the visitors take a 1-0 lead over the hosts! Another win will see them inch closer to a series win.
... MATCH DAY ...

We are here at the Kensington Oval in Bridgetown, Barbados, for the final time in this T20I series between England and West Indies before the action shifts to St Lucia for the remaining three T20Is. It was an action-packed series opener, with momentum shifting back and forth until England’s chase turned it into a one-sided show. Chasing 183, Phil Salt was electric at the top, blasting his way through the West Indies bowling attack with a ton. He was accompanied by Jacob Bethell as the duo guided England comfortably to the finish line. The joy of victory, however, was dampened by the sight of Reece Topley limping off after an unfortunate slip in his follow-through, casting doubt on his availability for the rest of the series. If Topley sits out, John Turner or Jofra Archer are likely candidates to step in for the left-arm quick. England will be keen to refine their death bowling, as it still has room for improvement. But the batting unit is on a high, having notched up the highest successful chase in T20Is at the Kensington Oval. On the other hand, the West Indies were rocked early in their innings but showed resilience, with the lower order fighting to put up a competitive score. They will likely keep playing fearless cricket but will be hoping one or two batters can convert starts into a big score to set them up for a stronger finish. In the bowling department, Shamar Joseph lacked the impact they would have hoped for, which could see Matthew Forde, who shined in the ODI series, slot in to add more bite to their attack in the next game. After taking a heavy toll from Salt and Bethell, the West Indies bowlers will be eager for a quick turnaround to put on a stronger display in the second T20I. Another exciting contest awaits as both teams look to assert themselves in this exciting series. Who are you backing to come out on top?
